trails.title: Shoeshine Boys
trails.description: Several boys, rubbing the shoe polish in their hands over and over on a towel, invite you to sit down.

content.text:
"Come, sir, put your feet up, please. I'll wipe the dust off your shoes, and we can even talk about the opera, if you'd like. The opera, yes! Isn't it just all over the posters, in the streets and alleys! Isn't it just, sir! Please, just a few more coins, sir, so that I can afford a ticket for tonight ... Of course, I understand, sir, I know all the lines off by heart! "Pourquoi faut-il que le destin l'ait mise là sur mon chemin?" I learned that off a kind gentleman outside the theater ..."

...

"You must try the Sachertorte—we say this to every tourist ... Haha, of course! How could I recommend it to you if I hadn't tasted it myself? Rest assured!"

...

"Look, sir! I bet you don't even recognize your shoes anymore! I can even see my face in them. I've polished them so hard ..."

"You must be here to see the sights of Vienna, right? The streets here are spotless, and after this polish, you won't have to clean your shoes for at least ten days ... Yes, if things carry on like this, we'll have to go to school. I hear they teach French there ... Next time you come to Vienna, maybe I'll be that little apprentice up on the stage."

items.text: Art Exhibit
From a higher vantage, the view is much improved.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Reporter of New Free Press, editor-in-chief of the Pan ... The founder of The Torch ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Oh, that's Egon Erwin Kisch! The reporter who uncovered the scandal surrounding Colonel Alfred Redl ... I had investigated this before ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Adolf Loos, the architect! He designed the Steiner House, as I recall. That's Major Maximilian Ronge and his wife ... who knew that celebrities like them would visit this exhibition.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But they look different from the pictures in the papers ... They were younger, and less chubby. Has my memory failed me? Or is it because photography is also an art of beautification?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Mr. Karl was right. People are flocking to the Secession Building to get a glimpse of the new art.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: … I can't appreciate these things at all.
Hofmann comments from her typical cold objectivity.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I've informed the Field Agent Squad, as soon as Heinrich shows up, we'll get him under control.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Ideally, we will take him away for "illegal use of arcane skills." It is the best reason and the least risk. It also complies with the laws of this time. If Manus Vindictae is behind all this, they'll show themselves for sure.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The squad will assist us from the perimeter by then.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Marcus, your mission is to watch everything closely. Heinrich could be disguised and hiding in the crowd. Also keep an eye on the Manus and their rituals—that's what we were originally here for.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Leave it to me! I won't miss a thing.
Marcus takes a deep breath, seeking a clear moment before diving.
A starburst of information floods into Marcus's eyes, reeling across her mind with a thousand pages at once.
The world has always been a book to her.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Mr. Thomas, the representative, is talking to the ladies about expressionism. His parents did not foresee the success of Impressionism—the works that made no sense but became priceless on the market.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: That's why his generation over-corrects their aesthetic standards and pays compliments to any art they don't understand.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: The reporter for the New Free Press and that major are discussing the frequent suicides in Vienna ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: They've written articles about it, and many of them attribute it to the publication of The Sorrows of Young Werther.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Kakania is describing the founding idea of "The Circle." "This is the first magic circle drawn by the primitive man!" Hmm, quite the strong woman ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: The military exercise in Bosnia and Herzegovina this spring ... General Conrad to lose power ... A low pressure trough on the Atlantic Ocean ... Ivory-colored paper for official use only ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: The general ... Wife of a cabinet member ... Quartz sand ... Is arcanum a bacterial infection ... Is psychoanalysis a new type of mental illness ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Mr. Heinrich is not here.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Nothing useful on this page.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Ah, Ms. Isolde again. She's the host of the exhibition.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: She seems ... healthier than the last time we met.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I don't know why, but I'm happy for her.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: She's about to make a speech.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: It is my honor to host this exhibition.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Before we begin, I'd like to express my gratitude for Mr. Heinrich, who is Theophil's friend and the curator of this exhibition.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Heinrich still hasn't shown up. Did he notice something?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: And also a friend of mine, the founder of "The Circle"—Ms. Klara!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Without her tireless work behind the scenes, we wouldn't be here today. Born into a rising arcane family of the middle class, Ms. Klara is a devoted doctor and an art connoisseur with impeccable taste.
Isolde makes for a dramatic introduction, reaching out towards the audience below.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Ugh!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Dr. Kakania is standing up, greeting the guests. That's an awkward smile. Looks like she didn't see this coming.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Hmm, Ms. Isolde is giving her an encouraging look. She wants to introduce her friend to the celebrities?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: So they're actually very close ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: *sigh* I told her not to mention my name ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Ms. Kakania is lowering her hat. Does she not like the spotlight? No, that's not it. Is it because of Ms. Dittarsdorf's gaze?
Marcus observes the woman in green intently.
Isolde lifts the curtain.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: This is the debut of The Salvation—the only painting Theophil left behind.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: This is it!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: In his last moments, Theophil became obsessed with the Golden Isle. He envisioned it as a realm of art and culture, a utopia for arcanists.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: There, the primal vitality and passion of arcanists would be preserved and never tainted by the outside world.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: He wrote, "That island holds the hope of salvation."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Hmm, is this so? This is above my clearance ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Sounds like everyone in Vienna has their own interpretation of the island.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Ladies and gentlemen, your attention please! We are forming a committee to petition the Empire to cease its attacks on the island!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: The arcanists there are not lunatics, they're simply living free!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Erm?!
Familiar words interrupt Marcus's thoughts, her eyes widening in bewilderment.
But beneath the spotlight, the speech continues.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Their existence is a revelation to us. To help them is to help ourselves.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Our society is sick. Treating the individual is only treating a symptom. It needs a radical surgery, a revolution that will let us rediscover our repressed nature, and reinvent ourselves in this world ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Something's wrong. Her speech is ...
Marcus's intuition hammers out a warning. A loud clear klaxon in her mind.
Before she can act, Isolde raises her hand as if holding out some drawn sword, reaching the climax of her speech.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I wish for the arcanists to unite ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: And establish an independent kingdom of freedom, free from repression and oppression!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: It's an emergency. Seal the exits. Add Isolde to our targets.
Hofmann delivers her orders coldly and without a moment of hesitation.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Marcus, now.

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: Am I hearing things, or did Ms. Dittarsdorf really say that?
At first, the crowd stirs like a ripple over a deep and swift current.

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: Forgive her! Perhaps Ms. Dittarsdorf hasn't fully recovered from her illness ...

items.speaker: Guest III
items.text: I think so too!
Kakania rises up from her seat, her hat sliding off her knee, stunned hands failing to catch it.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What, how? I did not tell her to ...

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Ladies and gentlemen! Dear friends! Calm down!
A man's voice booms from the other end of the exhibition hall.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Do not panic, for I have found salvation for you!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Heinrich? What is that behind you ...

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: Hofmann, the targets showed up! But golems are attacking us!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I see it too.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The arcane skill of object enchantment? Marcus, give it a read.
Armored statues surround Heinrich, reaching a motionless still that creates an odd, if dramatic, tableau.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Please do not ignore what Ms. Dattersdorf is saying! This is a proving ground of a world-ending experiment!

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: A catastrophe is coming. The clouds of war are filling up the sky.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Open your eyes and look at all we have now. The music, the art, the ambitions of progress ...

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Man's gunfire will destroy them all!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: ... What?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What ... are you all talking about?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Not to worry, doctor. You simply don't know yet.
The woman, now so strange in the doctor's eyes, reaches out her hand.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Follow me, and I'll show you everything, where your dream has taken root.
The appearance of the golems agitates the crowd, and the ripple becomes a chaotic crash of waves.

items.speaker: Guest III
items.text: This is ridiculous! An independent kingdom? It is treason!

items.speaker: Guest III
items.text: We are Viennese! Why would we want to leave our own country?

items.speaker: Guest IV
items.text: Are these golems works of art too? They look expensive, I'd like one in my collection.

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: Open the door and let us go! This travesty is a disgrace!
The glow of arcane skill strikes against the golem but leaves no trace of damage.

items.speaker: Team Member
items.text: D**n, are these golems immune to arcanum? We can't get to Heinrich!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Madam Hofmann, I read them! Object enchantment strokes, the same ones we found at the Foundation branch!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Any signs of the Manus's rituals?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: No, nothing yet.
Hofmann nods, pressing the communicator again.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text:
Golems can only be broken from within. Marcus, tell everyone the method.
Olla, evacuate everyone and use the mute spell. Don't let more people hear about the "era"!
The mentor, now agent, draws her sidearm, pushing through the panicked crowd.
Through the gaps between the golems, she keenly spots a pink dress disappearing behind a painting.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Heinrich's escaped with Isolde. There's an opening behind the painting.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: After them!
TO BE CONTINUED…
